topic: Autonomous Hill Development Councils expanded across Ladakh

subtopics.title: AHDCs versus 6th Schedule councils and Article 371
subtopics.summary: AHDCs and 6th Schedule Autonomous District Councils are both local bodies, but they differ in how they are created, where they apply and what powers they hold. AHDCs are created through legislation and apply only in Ladakh, while 6th Schedule councils have constitutional status under Articles 244(2) and 275(1). Article 371 and Articles 371A to 371J, under Part XXI, provide special safeguards for indigenous culture, customary laws, land rights and local employment.
facts: AHDCs: created through legislation and apply only in Ladakh
6th Schedule councils: constitutional status under Articles 244(2) and 275(1)
6th Schedule councils apply in notified tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura
AHDCs: mainly administrative and developmental powers, no judicial authority
6th Schedule councils: legislative, executive, financial and judicial powers
6th Schedule councils can establish village courts under customary tribal laws
Article 371 and Articles 371A to 371J fall under Part XXI
Article 371 aims to protect indigenous culture, customary laws, land rights, local employment, tribal identity and administrative autonomy

subtopics.title: Ladakh's profile, demands and 2025 reservation rules
subtopics.summary: Ladakh, known as the Land of High Passes or Maryul, has been administered by the Government of India as a Union Territory since 31 October 2019. Its people demand inclusion under the 6th Schedule, restrictions on land ownership to prevent outsider influx, and a Legislative Assembly. A reservation regulation approved on 2 June 2025 and effective from 3 June 2025 raises the total reservation cap to 85 per cent, with EWS quotas excluded.
facts: Known as the Land of High Passes, or Maryul
Administered by the Government of India as a UT since 31 October 2019
Capital: Leh, with Kargil as the winter capital
Demand: inclusion under the 6th Schedule for constitutional protection
Demand: land ownership restrictions to prevent outsider influx
Demand: a Legislative Assembly for representative governance
Effective from 3 June 2025; affects government jobs and educational admissions
Total reservation cap raised to 85 per cent, EWS quotas excluded
